extracted.intended_audience: U.S. Senators, congressional staff, patent policy stakeholders (industry, universities, independent inventors), and PTO/patent practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing legislative provisions and policy criteria in H.R.1249 (America Invents Act) covering PTO funding, procedural reforms (post‑grant review, first‑inventor‑to‑file), business‑method patent treatment, joinder rules, and related measures intended to improve patent quality and reduce backlog.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dedication of PTO user fees to PTO operation / prevent fee diversion
rubrics_metrics.description: “The fees that PTO collects to review and approve patent applications should be dedicated to PTO operation. However, fee diversion by Congress has hampered PTO’s efforts to hire and retain a sufficient number of qualified examiners and implement technological improvements necessary to ensure expeditious issuance of high quality patents.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion favors statutory and/or structural protections that ensure user fees paid to the USPTO are available to the PTO to hire examiners, modernize systems, and reduce backlog rather than being diverted to other government uses. The text cites historical diversion amounts and links diversion to increased pendency and reduced patent quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce backlog and patent pendency
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduce the backlog of pending applications and shorten pendency time (cites backlog of 1.2 million applications waiting for a final determination and pendency time of three years; elsewhere FY2010 pendency 35.3 months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures should be judged on whether they materially speed examination (e.g., hiring examiners, process improvements) and reduce time-to-grant. The record links pendency metrics directly to fee availability and PTO resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide PTO access to collected fees (reserve fund / fee-setting authority)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions that authorize the PTO to set its fees and establish a Patent and Trademark Fee Reserve Fund so fees collected in excess of appropriations remain available for PTO use; debate over language that would permit Director use 'without fiscal year limitation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between mere creation of an account/fund versus statutory language that guarantees access to funds without appropriation constraints. Supporters argue fund + fee‑setting will let PTO implement reforms; critics warn House language still defers to appropriations and may not stop diversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: First‑inventor‑to‑file system
rubrics_metrics.description: The bill 'shifts the U.S. to a first‑inventor‑to‑file system that the Chamber believes is both constitutional and wise, ending expensive interference proceedings.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion evaluates moving from a prior‑inventor to first‑to‑file regime to reduce interference proceedings and provide clearer priority rules. Consider constitutional, practical, and litigation‑cost impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: End frivolous false patent marking cases while preserving actual‑harm suits (Section 16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 16 would put an end to frivolous false patent marking cases, while still preserving the right of those who suffered actual harm to bring actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy should limit opportunistic/abusive marking suits but preserve remedies for parties who can show real harm. Evaluate whether statutory language accomplishes that balance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create prior user right for early commercial users (Section 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 5 would create a prior user right for those who first commercially use inventions, protecting the rights of early inventors and giving manufacturers a powerful incentive to build new factories in the United States, while at the same time fully protecting universities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion assesses whether the bill protects commercial users who began practicing an invention before a later patent application, balancing manufacturing incentives with university tech‑transfer concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrict joinder of tenuously connected defendants (Section 19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 19 also restricts joinder of defendants who have tenuous connections to the underlying disputes in patent infringement suits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates whether the joinder rules prevent plaintiffs from aggregating unrelated defendants into single suits, thereby reducing abusive or opportunistic litigation strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailored pilot program for patent office expert review of business method patents (Section 18)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 18 provides for a tailored pilot program which would allow patent office experts to help the court review the validity of certain business method patents using the best available prior art as an alternative to costly litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports administrative/court assistance using PTO expertise and prior‑art searches as an alternative to lengthy litigation; judge effect on cost, speed, and patent quality for business method patents should be measured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative pre‑litigation determination for business method patents (Senate Section 18 language)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Senate language would have the Patent Office make an administrative determination before the years of litigation as to whether this patent is a legitimate patent so as not to allow the kind of abuse we have seen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion favors an administrative filter for business method patents to resolve patent legitimacy early; opponents worry House wording broadens scope (e.g., inserting 'other' and extending 8 years) and could cancel already‑issued patents and cause chaos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit scope/duration of administrative review to avoid disrupting issued patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Concerns that the House language, by adding the word 'other,' broadens the definition of section 18 and extends it for 8 years, potentially allowing cancellation of patents already issued by the Patent Office and throwing into disarray companies that believe they have legitimate patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess proposed text for overbreadth and retroactive effects on issued patents; safeguard stability of issued rights while enabling review of problematic patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent abusive business method patents and reduce related litigation costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Business method patents are criticized as improper (example: 'double click'); administrative review is proposed so that opponents get an early chance to weigh in and avoid costly litigation concentrated in plaintiff‑friendly districts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate reforms on whether they reduce abusive patents, lower litigation cost/time (currently 'about 10 years' and 'tens of millions of dollars'), and curb forum shopping (e.g., Eastern District of Texas).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure reforms do not unduly reduce appropriations oversight / preserve accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Opposition notes that establishing an off‑budget revolving fund would put the PTO on 'autopilot' without the oversight of an annual legislative vehicle to hold the agency accountable; appropriations oversight has been used to force management reforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance criterion: provide PTO predictable access to fees to perform duties while retaining sufficient congressional oversight to ensure accountability and guard against misuse or funding shortfalls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require funding adequacy to implement new post‑grant procedures (budgetary impact)
rubrics_metrics.description: CBO estimates: the new post‑grant review procedure would cost $140 million to implement over 10 years; the new supplemental review procedure $758 million; inter partes reexamination changes $251 million; total over $1 billion over 10 years. Without access to fees, these costs could worsen pendency and undermine patent quality improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion assesses whether the bill provides realistic, protected funding sufficient to implement new procedures and related PTO obligations identified by budgetary analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify procedural deadlines to prevent arbitrary administrative application
rubrics_metrics.description: Language (section 37 debate) intended to 'guarantee in the future that no bureaucrat can act in an arbitrary and capricious way when they decide when does the 60‑day period of time start.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion demands statutory clarity so that filing and response deadlines are applied uniformly and not subject to inconsistent administrative interpretations that can deny parties rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reform damages calculation and publication requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholders were 'principally concerned with issues dealing with how damages are calculated for infringed patents, new post‑grant review procedures, and publication requirements for pending patents.' H.R.1249 'satisfactorily addresses these issues' according to some stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether statutory changes to damages rules and publication practices improve predictability, fairness, and technology transfer without enabling abuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support independent inventors by increasing speed and certainty
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent inventors urge passage because the legislation 'will give independent inventors and entrepreneurs the speed and certainty necessary to go out and commercialize their inventions, start companies, and create jobs.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion measures reforms by their concrete effect on small inventors: faster decisions, predictable rights, and reduced litigation barriers that allow commercialization and company formation.
